output.name: Skelmi

anatomy.part: belly, at the hip of the body
chest, where the right wing is set
right wing, at the elbow of the leading edge
trailing foot, hanging down and left

output.myth: Ennu sat on the cliff with a bone needle and a bolt of sailcloth, making a gull for a woman whose husband had gone out in a boat and not come back. He sewed the body first, then the left wing, then the right, and he was on the last feather when the woman died under the smoke-hole. Ennu did not finish the bird. He tied off the thread and set it on the wind, and Tavo, who laughs at unfinished things, took it up and carried it past the Leeward Reach. Hesk counted the stitches as it went. There are a hundred and forty of them, she says, and one gap where the thread should have run. The gull is in the Unflown now, one wing open like a question. Sailors who see it say it will not come home, and that is no fault of the wind. Grandmothers say to leave one loose stitch in every kite you make, so the thing you made has somewhere to go back to.
output.verse:
Gull with one wing bare,
still open toward the south—
the thread still hangs loose.
